Subsides.name: Minimum Support Price (MSP) Increase for Wheat
Subsides.description: The Indian government raised the MSP for new-season wheat by 150 rupees per 100 kg, a 6.6% increase, setting it at 2,425 rupees per 100 kg for the 2025 season. This move aims to incentivize farmers to expand wheat cultivation and reduce dependency on imports.

Subsides.name: Fertilizer Subsidy Allocation
Subsides.description: In the federal budget for the financial year 2025-26, the Indian government allocated 1.67 trillion rupees for fertilizer subsidies. This allocation aims to support farmers by reducing the cost of fertilizers, thereby promoting agricultural productivity.

Subsides.name: Interest Subvention Scheme for Crop Loans
Subsides.description: The government provides interest subvention on short-term crop loans up to ₹3 lakh, offering loans to farmers at a subsidized interest rate. This initiative aims to ensure the availability of affordable credit to the agriculture sector.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Micro-Irrigation under PMKSY
Subsides.description: Under the 'Per Drop More Crop' component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY), the government offers subsidies for micro-irrigation systems, including drip and sprinkler irrigation, to promote efficient water usage in agriculture.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Organic Farming under PKVY
Subsides.description: The Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) promotes organic farming through financial assistance for organic inputs, certification, and training. This subsidy encourages sustainable agricultural practices among farmers.

Subsides.name: Fertilizer Subsidy Reduction for Rabi Season
Subsides.description: The Indian Union Cabinet reduced the subsidy on fertilizers containing nitrogen and sulfur for the Rabi season (October 2024 to March 2025). This adjustment aims to rationalize subsidy expenditure and promote balanced fertilizer usage.

Subsides.name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Enhancement
Subsides.description: The budget allocation for the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund was increased to ₹900 crore in 2024-25. This fund provides financial support for the development of agricultural infrastructure projects at the farm gate and aggregation points.

Subsides.name: Modified Interest Subvention Scheme
Subsides.description: An allocation of ₹22,600 crore was made for the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, which aims to provide short-term credit to farmers at subsidized interest rates, ensuring timely credit availability for agricultural operations.

Subsides.name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS) for Middle Income Group (MIG)
Subsides.description: The government allocated ₹1,000 crore for the CLSS, aiming to provide interest subsidies on housing loans to middle-income groups, indirectly benefiting rural populations, including farmers.

Subsides.name: Interest Subsidy Scheme for EWS/LIG
Subsides.description: An allocation of ₹2,500 crore was made for the Interest Subsidy Scheme targeting Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low-Income Groups (LIG), facilitating affordable housing through subsidized interest rates.

Subsides.name: Income Support under PM-KISAN
Subsides.description: The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme provides income support of ₹6,000 per year to small and marginal farmer families, payable in three equal installments. This initiative aims to supplement farmers' financial needs for procuring inputs.

Subsides.name: Food Subsidy Allocation
Subsides.description: In the federal budget for 2025-26, the Indian government allocated 2.03 trillion rupees for food subsidies. This allocation ensures the availability of food grains at affordable prices to the economically disadvantaged sections of society.

Subsides.name: Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme Allocation
Subsides.description: The government allocated 860 billion rupees for the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) scheme in the 2025-26 budget. This scheme provides at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households, enhancing livelihood security.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Crop Insurance under PMFBY
Subsides.description: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) offers premium subsidies for crop insurance, protecting farmers against potential crop losses due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases. Farmers pay a maximum premium of 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial or horticultural crops, with the remaining premium subsidized by the government. The scheme also covers post-harvest losses and utilizes technology-driven assessments for accurate and timely claim settlements.

Subsides.name: Fertilizer Subsidy
Subsides.description: The Government of India provides subsidies to fertilizer manufacturers to ensure that fertilizers are available to farmers at affordable prices, thereby promoting agricultural productivity.

Subsides.name: Electricity Subsidy
Subsides.description: State governments offer subsidized electricity rates to farmers for agricultural purposes, particularly for operating irrigation pumps, to reduce the cost of cultivation.

Subsides.name: Irrigation Subsidy
Subsides.description: Financial assistance is provided for the development and maintenance of irrigation infrastructure, including canals and tube wells, to ensure adequate water supply for farming.

Subsides.name: Interest Subsidy on Crop Loans
Subsides.description: The government offers interest subvention on short-term crop loans to ensure farmers have access to credit at reduced interest rates, aiding in timely agricultural operations.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Agricultural Equipment
Subsides.description: To promote mechanization, subsidies are provided for purchasing agricultural machinery and equipment, enhancing efficiency and reducing labor costs.

Subsides.name: Seed Subsidy
Subsides.description: Financial support is extended to farmers for purchasing high-quality seeds, ensuring better crop yields and productivity.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Cold Storage Facilities
Subsides.description: Assistance is provided for the establishment of cold storage units to reduce post-harvest losses and maintain the quality of perishable agricultural produce.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Organic Farming
Subsides.description: Incentives are offered to farmers adopting organic farming practices, including financial support for organic inputs and certification processes.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Solar Pumps
Subsides.description: Under the PM-KUSUM scheme, farmers receive subsidies to install solar-powered pumps, reducing dependence on conventional energy sources and promoting sustainable irrigation.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Micro-Irrigation Systems
Subsides.description: Financial assistance is provided for the installation of micro-irrigation systems like drip and sprinkler irrigation, promoting water-use efficiency.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Plant Protection Chemicals
Subsides.description: Support is extended for purchasing pesticides and other plant protection chemicals to safeguard crops from pests and diseases.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Soil Health Management
Subsides.description: Financial assistance is provided for soil testing and the implementation of soil health improvement measures, ensuring sustainable fertility management.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Agricultural Extension Services
Subsides.description: Support is provided for training and capacity-building programs aimed at educating farmers on modern agricultural practices and technologies.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Horticulture Development
Subsides.description: Financial assistance is extended for the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, and other horticultural crops, including support for infrastructure development.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Livestock Farming
Subsides.description: Incentives are provided for livestock rearing, including support for the purchase of high-yielding breeds and the construction of shelters.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Fisheries Development
Subsides.description: Financial support is offered for aquaculture and fisheries, including assistance for pond construction and the purchase of fishing equipment.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Beekeeping
Subsides.description: Support is provided for apiculture activities, including assistance for the procurement of bee colonies and hives, promoting pollination and honey production.

Subsides.name: Subsidy for Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure
Subsides.description: Financial assistance is extended for the development of marketing infrastructure, such as warehouses and cold chains, to facilitate better market access for farmers.

Subsides.name: Subsidy on Crop Diversification
Subsides.description: The Crop Diversification Programme (CDP), initiated in 2013-14 as a sub-scheme of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY), aims to encourage farmers in Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh to shift from water-intensive crops like paddy to alternatives such as maize, pulses, oilseeds, cotton, and agro-forestry. The program provides financial assistance for cluster demonstrations, promotion of water-saving technologies, distribution of farm machinery, establishment of value addition facilities, and farmer training programs.
